parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Using the data in Table 1.1, calculate the price elasticity of demand (PED) for nickel between
2022 and the forecast for 2024.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
State what this estimate suggests about the PED for nickel and why this estimate might be
considered ‘highly unusual’.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
With the help of a demand and supply diagram, explain the effect of a subsidy on
the production of nickel in Australia and consider whether the impact will always be
as expected.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
‘The Australian government plans a large increase in its spending.’
Assess the possible effects of a large increase in government spending by the government
on the Australian economy.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Assess whether the principle of comparative advantage should be the only factor to consider
when the Australian government decides whether to support the production of nickel.

parts.text:
Explain, using examples, the difference between a public good and a merit good and
consider the extent to which an increase in the provision of information on the benefits of a
merit good is the best way to increase its consumption.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Assess the extent to which the nature of public goods means that they can only ever be
provided in a mixed economy. 
Or

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain, with the help of a diagram, what is meant by market equilibrium and consider the
extent to which changes in the level of consumer income will change the market price for
a product.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Assess the extent to which government intervention to control prices in a market can cause
changes in both the amount of quantity demanded and quantity supplied of a product in
that market. 
Section C
Answer one question.
Either

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain why economic growth is usually measured using real GDP rather than nominal GDP
and consider the extent to which an economy can only achieve economic growth by an
increase in the quantity of its resources.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Assess the extent to which the benefits of economic growth will always outweigh the costs
for all economies. 
Or

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
With the help of a diagram, explain the circular flow of income in an open economy with
government intervention and consider the extent to which the level of income in this
economy may change following its transition to a closed economy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Assess the extent to which a government can use fiscal policy to influence leakages
from and injections into the circular flow of income to achieve any two of its
macroeconomic objectives.
